prompt: A pattern: $1 \to 5$, $2 \to 9$, $3 \to 13$. What is the rule (as $y = $ expression)?
hint: Look at how much the output grows each time the input goes up by $1$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try the pattern $1 \to 4$, $2 \to 8$, $3 \to 12$ first. Its rule is $y = 4x$. How are the outputs in this problem different from those?
Look at how much the output grows each time the input goes up by $1$.
The outputs $5, 9, 13$ go up by $4$ each time, so the rule starts with $4x$. Compare $4 \times 1$ with the real output $5$ to find what must be added.
$4(1) = 4$ is one short of $5$, so the rule is $y=4x+1$.

explanation: Each time $x$ goes up by $1$, the output goes up by $4$ (from $5$ to $9$ to $13$), so $x$ is multiplied by $4$.
Test $4x$ alone on the first pair: $4(1) = 4$, but the output is $5$, so $1$ more is needed.
That suggests the rule is $y = 4x + 1$, but it should be tested.
Check the other pairs: $4(2) + 1 = 9$ and $4(3) + 1 = 13$. The rule is $y = 4x + 1$.
